title: Lord of Mercy, at Thy Gate
description: Lord of Mercy, at Thy Gate in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens (7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord of mer-cy, at Thy gate, Nee-dy souls im-plor-ing pray; Have we come, Good Lord, too late? Must we turn in grief a-way?

lines: Lord of mercy, at Thy gate,
Needy souls imploring pray;
Have we come, Good Lord, too late?
Must we turn in grief away?
Young and old Thy mercy claim, —
Some are early at the gate,
Some are late to own Thy name,
Surely none, though late, too late!
Blessed, who with morning sun,
Hopeful at Thy portals wait;
Yea, and when the day is done,
Blessed they who find the gate.
Ah, Good Lord, when Thou wert here,
Homeless, in our world of sin,
Few, to give Thee warmth and cheer,
Called their weary Lord within.
Sad, repenting, full of fear,
Hoping, doubting, still we wait;
As we call, in mercy hear; —
Open, Lord, to us the gate.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
